Alloys with nominal compositions of Ni48Co24Cr24–Nb4, Ni48Co22Cr22–Nb4V4 and Ni47Co22Cr22–Nb4V4Ta1 (at.%) were prepared by vacuum arc melting under argon atmosphere. The purity of raw materials used in this work were higher than 99.95 wt%. Melting was repeated at least 5 times to ensure the chemical homogeneity, and ingots were flipped before each re-melting.
The cast ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 6 h and subsequently sectioned into pieces with a thickness of 14 mm using an Electro-Discharged Machine (EDM).
The 14 mm pieces were cold-rolled down to 2 mm for a total reduction of 85%,

and recrystallized at 1150 °C for 7 min. Recrystallized samples were further aged at 800 °C for 5–1000 h with the purpose of introducing nano ε plates and nano-twins. All heat treatments were conducted in air, as the alloy samples are oxidation-resistant due to high Cr content, followed by quickly quenching into ice water to maintain the microstructure at high-temperature.

Recrystallized samples were further aged at 800 °C for 5–1000 h with the purpose of introducing nano ε plates and nano-twins. The results suggest that Ni, Nb and Ta primarily partition into the ε phase, while Co and Cr are enriched in the γ matrix.

The results suggest that Ni, Nb and Ta primarily partition into the ε phase, while Co and Cr are enriched in the γ matrix. V is evenly distributed in γ and ε, without obvious segregations. Based on the EDS results of precipitates compositions (as shown in Table 1) and the reported substitution behavior of alloying elements in ε phase [17], the chemical formula of ε phase in NVT800 can be expressed as (Ni, Co, Cr)3(Nb, V, Ta).
Compared to the N800 alloy (Fig. 1(a–c)), the addition of V significantly increases the volume fraction of ε plates, as shown in Fig. 1(d–f).
while V addition increases the volume fraction up to ~31% and reduces lamellar spacing down to ~161 nm.
The crystallographic orientation relationship between γ phase and ε precipitates is determined on the basis of SAD pattern, which can be expressed as: {111}γ//(0001)ε and <110>γ//[12 10]ε.
The thickness of ε plates is measured to be ~42 nm according to image analysis.
The volume fraction of ε plates in N800 is about ~14% and the lamellar spacing is about ~200 nm;
while V addition increases the volume fraction up to ~31% and reduces lamellar spacing down to ~161 nm.

For reproducibility, at least 50 areas were carefully observed, and a sandwiched nano-twin (thickness ranging from 2 to 17 nm) is found between each γ matrix and aligned ε plates. HR-TEM images of different sizes of nano-twins are also shown in Supplementary Information Fig. S5.
As a result, a nano-twin/ε plates/nano-twin sandwich heterostructure is embedded within the γ matrix. The schematic for this double-stacked-sandwich hetero-nanostructure is presented in Fig. 4(b).

The presented results prove that precipitation of plate-like ε phase can also increase the hardness of NiCoCr-based alloys significantly.

Moreover, the boundaries of nano-twins with a thickness of a few nanometers have been reported to be effective barriers to dislocation slip, while they can also provide room for dislocation accumulation and storage [29].

The hardness values of the solid-solution (single phase) N800, NV800 and NVT800 alloys (aging time of 0 h) are almost the same, indicating the addition of V and/or Ta do not contribute to obvious solid solution strengthening.

The XRD pattern (Fig. 3(d)) further confirms that the plate-like precipitates in the aged NVT800 are ε phase, which is consistent with previous research [36].
For reproducibility, at least 50 areas were carefully observed, and a sandwiched nano-twin (thickness ranging from 2 to 17 nm) is found between each γ matrix and aligned ε plates.
As a result, a nano-twin/ε plates/nano-twin sandwich heterostructure is embedded within the γ matrix. The schematic for this double-stacked-sandwich hetero-nanostructure is presented in Fig. 4(b).

Moreover, the boundaries of nano-twins with a thickness of a few nanometers have been reported to be effective barriers to dislocation slip, while they can also provide room for dislocation accumulation and storage [29].
The presented results prove that precipitation of plate-like ε phase can also increase the hardness of NiCoCr-based alloys significantly.

The nano-twin formation can improve strengths at elevated temperatures (~725 °C), and does not compromise other properties such as low-cycle fatigue life, crack-growth rate and hot workability [39,40].
